audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph temple donations, David's prayer, Solomon's anointing, sacrifices, succession, and David's death, first-pass restored draft; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Solomon's youth, royal and public giving, voluntary-offering pressure, source of wealth, hyperbolic totals, stewardship prayer, sojourner identity, integrity, animal sacrifice, bowing to king, throne-of-YHWH language, idealized submission, Davidic absolution, and lost archives.

verses.restored: King David said to all assembly, Solomon my son, whom alone Divine has chosen, is young and inexperienced, and work is great, for palace is not for human but for YHWH Divine.

With all strength I prepared for house of Divine: gold for gold work, silver for silver, bronze for bronze, iron for iron, wood for wood, onyx and setting stones, stones of antimony and colors, every precious stone, and marble in abundance.
Moreover, because I delight in house of my Divine, I give my personal treasure of gold and silver to house of Divine beyond all prepared for holy house:
three thousand talents of gold, gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver to overlay walls of houses,
gold for gold work, silver for silver work, and for all work by hands of artisans. Who then offers willingly to fill hand today for YHWH?
Then leaders of ancestral houses, tribal leaders, commanders of thousands and hundreds, and officials over king's work offered willingly.

They gave for service of house of Divine five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and one hundred thousand talents of iron.
Whoever had precious stones gave them to treasury of house of YHWH under hand of Jehiel the Gershonite.
People rejoiced because they offered willingly, for with whole heart they offered to YHWH; David the king also rejoiced greatly.
David blessed YHWH before all assembly, saying, Blessed are you, YHWH Divine of Israel our ancestor, from age to age.
Yours, YHWH, are greatness, power, glory, victory, and majesty, for all in heavens and earth is yours. Yours is kingdom, YHWH, and you are lifted as head above all.
Riches and honor come from before you, and you rule over all; in your hand are power and might, and in your hand to make great and strengthen all.
Now, our Divine, we thank you and praise your glorious name.
Who am I and who are my people that we should have strength to offer willingly like this? For all is from you, and from your hand we have given to you.
For we are sojourners before you and temporary residents, as all ancestors; our days on earth are like shadow, and there is no lasting hope in possession.
YHWH our Divine, all this abundance prepared to build house for holy name is from your hand, and all is yours.
I know, my Divine, you test heart and delight in uprightness. In uprightness of heart I willingly offered all these, and now I have seen your people present offering willingly with joy.
YHWH Divine of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel our ancestors, keep this forever as formation of thoughts of heart of your people, and establish their heart toward you.
Give Solomon my son a whole heart to guard commandments, testimonies, and statutes, to do all and build palace for which I prepared.
David said to all assembly, Bless YHWH your Divine. All assembly blessed YHWH Divine of ancestors and bowed, paying homage to YHWH and king.
They brought sacrifices to YHWH and offered burnt offerings next day: one thousand bulls, one thousand rams, one thousand lambs, with drink offerings and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
They ate and drank before YHWH that day with great joy. They made Solomon son of David king a second time and anointed him to YHWH as ruler, and Zadok as priest.
Solomon sat on throne of YHWH as king in place of David his father and prospered; all Israel obeyed him.
All leaders, mighty warriors, and also all sons of king David gave hand/submitted to Solomon the king.
YHWH magnified Solomon exceedingly in eyes of all Israel and put upon him royal majesty not seen on any king before in Israel.
David son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
Days he reigned over Israel were forty years: seven in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem.
He died at good old age, full of days, riches, and honor; Solomon his son reigned in his place.
Acts of David the king, first and last, are written in words of Samuel the seer, Nathan the prophet, and Gad the seer,
with all his reign and might and times that passed over him, Israel, and all kingdoms of lands.

translation_notes: Solomon is again called young and inexperienced before an enormous public project and succession ceremony; public acclaim does not prove uncoerced consent.
David's personal and royal wealth came through taxation, tribute, plunder, land, labor, and administration. Donation does not erase how wealth was accumulated.
The invitation to offer 'willingly' occurs in a royal public assembly after the king gives extravagantly; social and political pressure must be acknowledged.
The immense totals may be rhetorical or textually unstable and must not justify prosperity preaching or institutional hoarding.
Artisans' hands are named as the destination of materials; workers remain agents entitled to pay, safety, rest, and credit.
David's prayer that all belongs to Divine should support stewardship and humility, not institutional seizure of personal property.
Calling the community sojourners and temporary residents should cultivate hospitality toward migrants and loosen possessive nationalism.
Heart-testing belongs to Divine theology and cannot authorize leaders to police thoughts or demand financial proof of sincerity.
The assembly bows to YHWH and king in one verse; homage to a ruler is not worship and must not become leader cult.
Three thousand animals are killed in the ceremony; their lives and labor around the feast remain visible.
'Throne of YHWH' is royal theology, not a claim that monarchs are Divine or beyond removal.
All David's sons submitting to Solomon idealizes succession and omits Adonijah's conflict from Kings.
David's good death, wealth, and honor do not absolve Bathsheba's abuse, Uriah's murder, Tamar's abandonment, wars, census deaths, or other harms.
The cited prophetic records are not preserved as separate complete books; archival claims require humility.
safety_note: Reject coerced giving, prosperity fundraising, wealth laundering, leader worship, divine monarchy, thought policing, animal invisibility, and the absolution of David by a good ending. Center voluntary consent, migrants, artisans, financial transparency, Solomon's youth, and the survivors omitted from the closing celebration.
